_about: The institutions list behind pages/institutions.html and the Institutions grammar (grammars/institutions-of-alignment/grammar.json, built from this file by scripts/build_institutions_grammar.py). Hand-kept: edit this file, then run python scripts/build_all.py. Each `what_it_does` is paraphrased from the organisation's own pages as they read on the `checked` date; `raw_category` is the researcher's label, `group` the normalised one the page shows. Listing is not endorsement; nothing is ranked.
method: Every URL fetched with a browser user agent (HEAD, then GET when HEAD did not answer 200); every one answered 200 on the checked date.

groups.name: Democratic and cooperative alignment
groups.about: Work on aligning AI with what many people want, through public input, deliberation tools, or research on cooperation between AI systems.

groups.name: Field-building, grants and partnerships
groups.about: Organisations that fund, convene or build the field: grants, open letters, benchmarks, and partnerships across sectors.

groups.name: Forecasting and data
groups.about: Trends, datasets and scenario forecasts about where AI is heading.

groups.name: Governance and policy research
groups.about: Research meant for decision-makers: how advanced AI might be governed, and what its security implications are.

groups.name: Government bodies
groups.about: Public institutions that test AI systems, set standards or implement law.

groups.name: Humane technology
groups.about: Work on the harms of persuasive technology and on technology that serves people's wellbeing, now extending to AI.

groups.name: Public-interest research
groups.about: Independent research on the social effects of AI and data, often centred on people most affected by them.

groups.name: Technical alignment research
groups.about: Research on making AI systems do what their developers and users intend, and on understanding and overseeing what they do.

groups.name: Testing and evaluation
groups.about: Measuring what AI systems can do, and whether they behave safely, before and after release.

institutions.name: Center for Humane Technology
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit that brings to light the harms of persuasive technology and social media and helps people act on them; its current work extends to AI.
institutions.founded: 2018 (its site: Tristan Harris and two fellow technologists founded CHT in 2018)

institutions.name: AI Now Institute
institutions.what_it_does: An independent research institute producing diagnosis and policy research that questions and seeks to reimagine the current trajectory of AI.

institutions.name: Ada Lovelace Institute
institutions.what_it_does: An independent research institute whose mission is to make data and AI work for people and society.
institutions.founded: 2018 (its site: established by the Nuffield Foundation in early 2018)

institutions.name: Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR)
institutions.what_it_does: A globally distributed, independent group of academics, activists and engineers doing community-rooted AI research grounded in lived experience.

institutions.name: Algorithmic Justice League
institutions.what_it_does: Combines art and research to show the social implications and harms of AI, and works toward more equitable and accountable systems.

institutions.name: Collective Intelligence Project
institutions.what_it_does: Works to steer transformative AI toward better outcomes for everyone, using public input: alignment assemblies, global dialogues and community-built evaluations.

institutions.name: AI Objectives Institute
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit research and development lab (founded by the late Peter Eckersley) working so that AI, markets and institutions serve genuine human objectives, informed by broad public input.

one_thing_it_made.title: Talk to the City (open-source deliberation tool)

institutions.name: Meaning Alignment Institute
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit researching how to align AI, markets and democracies with what people value, an approach it calls full-stack alignment.

one_thing_it_made.title: What are human values, and how do we align AI to them? (2024)

institutions.name: Cooperative AI Foundation
institutions.what_it_does: A UK charity whose mission is to support research that improves the cooperative intelligence of advanced AI for the benefit of all.

one_thing_it_made.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI (2025 report)

institutions.name: Alignment Research Center (ARC)
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit research organization aiming to align future machine-learning systems with human interests; its current focus is a theoretical basis for mechanistic explanations of neural-network behaviour.

institutions.name: Redwood Research
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit AI safety and security research organization studying risks from AI systems that might act against their developers, and methods to manage those risks.

one_thing_it_made.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion

institutions.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit focused on preventing human extinction from artificial superintelligence; an early alignment research group that now also works on public communication and technical governance.
institutions.founded: 2000 (its site: founded as the Singularity Institute for Artificial Intelligence)

also.title: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies (book)

institutions.name: Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI), UC Berkeley
institutions.what_it_does: A multi-institution research group based at UC Berkeley working to reorient AI research toward provably beneficial systems.

institutions.name: FAR.AI
institutions.what_it_does: An AI safety and security research nonprofit working on robustness, deception and red-teaming, and on getting research results adopted.

institutions.name: Transluce
institutions.what_it_does: An independent nonprofit research lab building public tools and infrastructure for understanding and overseeing AI systems in the public interest.

one_thing_it_made.title: Docent (tool for analysing AI agent behaviour)

institutions.name: LawZero
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit developing technical approaches for capable, safe-by-design AI, with research direction led by Yoshua Bengio; incubated at Mila - Quebec AI Institute.

one_thing_it_made.title: Superintelligent Agents Pose Catastrophic Risks: Can Scientist AI Offer a Safer Path? (2025)

institutions.name: METR
institutions.what_it_does: A research nonprofit that measures whether and when AI systems' autonomous capabilities might threaten catastrophic harm.

one_thing_it_made.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks (2025)

institutions.name: Apollo Research
institutions.what_it_does: Focuses on reducing risks from 'scheming' frontier AI through evaluations, research and governance advice; announced in Sep 2026 that it is becoming a public benefit corporation.

one_thing_it_made.title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-Context Scheming

institutions.name: Palisade Research
institutions.what_it_does: A Berkeley nonprofit studying the capabilities and motivations of AI agents, to help people and institutions avoid losing control to them.

institutions.name: Humane Intelligence
institutions.what_it_does: A 501(c)(3) nonprofit that designs and runs collaborative evaluations (red-teaming, bias bounties) to make AI systems more accountable and fair.
institutions.founded: 2023 (its site: incorporated as a nonprofit in May 2023)

institutions.name: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
institutions.what_it_does: Helps decision-makers navigate the transition to advanced AI through research and by developing talent.
institutions.founded: 2016 (its site: founded at Yale; independent nonprofit since 2021)

one_thing_it_made.title: Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety (2023, multi-author, GovAI researchers among them)

institutions.name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), Georgetown
institutions.what_it_does: A policy research organization within Georgetown's Walsh School of Foreign Service offering data-driven, nonpartisan analysis of the security implications of emerging technologies, currently AI and advanced computing.

institutions.name: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
institutions.what_it_does: A research organisation within the UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology that tests leading AI systems before and after release to build governments' understanding of advanced-AI risks.

institutions.name: Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), NIST
institutions.what_it_does: A US government centre within NIST acting as industry's main point of contact for AI testing, developing measurement guidelines and evaluating demonstrable risks such as cyber, bio and chemical.

one_thing_it_made.title: CAISI Evaluation of DeepSeek V4 Pro (May 2026)

institutions.name: European AI Office
institutions.what_it_does: A European Commission office that supports the development and adoption of trustworthy AI while protecting people against its risks.

institutions.name: Epoch AI
institutions.what_it_does: A research institute investigating the trends and questions that shape AI's trajectory and governance, aiming for a neutral, evidence-based view.
institutions.founded: 2022 (its site: began 2021 as volunteers; founded after its 2022 compute-trends paper)

institutions.name: AI Futures Project
institutions.what_it_does: Publishes interactive scenario forecasts of AI's trajectory, with policy recommendations.

institutions.name: Future of Life Institute
institutions.what_it_does: Works to steer transformative technologies away from extreme, large-scale risks and toward benefiting life; known for the Asilomar AI Principles.

also.title: Pause Giant AI Experiments open letter (2023)

institutions.name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
institutions.what_it_does: Works to reduce societal-scale risks from AI through safety research, building the field of safety researchers, and promoting safety standards.

institutions.name: Partnership on AI
institutions.what_it_does: A nonprofit partnership of academic, civil-society, industry and media organizations creating solutions so AI advances positive outcomes for people and society; says it is not a trade group or advocacy organization.
institutions.founded: not stated; site marks its tenth anniversary in 2026

also.title: Deployment Guidance for Foundation Model Safety
